q: In Grade 10, one dimensional motion such as ____ and free fall motion was studied.
e: One-dimensional motion includes linear motion and free fall motion, which are the simplest types of motion encountered in many cases.

q: It is expected that students will examine two-dimensional motion; projectile and ____ motion.
e: The learning outcomes for this chapter include examining projectile and circular motion as key cases of two-dimensional motion.

q: In this chapter we will consider motion in two dimensions (or) motion in a ____.
e: Two-dimensional motion is also referred to as motion in a plane, where an object moves in both x and y directions simultaneously.

q: The object may move in both the x and ____ direction simultaneously.
e: In two-dimensional motion, the object's movement is described using both horizontal (x) and vertical (y) directions.

q: In order to describe the motion of an object in two dimensions, ____ concept must be used.
e: Vector concepts are essential for describing two-dimensional motion because both magnitude and direction must be accounted for.

q: The object moves along a ____ path between points P and Q as shown in Figure 1.1.
e: In two-dimensional motion, the object typically moves along a curved path rather than a straight line.

q: The displacement vector of the object from P to Q is ____.
e: The displacement vector $\Delta \vec{r}$ represents the change in position of the object from point P to point Q.

q: The perpendicular components of $\Delta \vec{r}$ are ____ and $\Delta y$.
e: The displacement vector can be resolved into perpendicular horizontal ($\Delta x$) and vertical ($\Delta y$) components.

q: The magnitude of $\Delta \vec{r}$ is given by $|\Delta \vec{r}| = $ ____.
e: The magnitude of the displacement vector is found using the Pythagorean theorem on its perpendicular components.

q: To find the direction of $\Delta \vec{r}$, $\tan \theta = $ ____.
e: The direction of the displacement vector is determined by the inverse tangent of the ratio of its y-component to its x-component.

q: Average velocity is defined as $\vec{v}_{avg} = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} $ ____.
e: Average velocity is the ratio of the change in displacement to the change in time as the time interval approaches zero.

q: Instantaneous velocity is defined as $\vec{v} = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \vec{r}}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous velocity is the derivative of the position vector with respect to time.

q: Average acceleration is given by $\vec{a}_{avg} = $ ____.
e: Average acceleration is the ratio of the change in velocity to the time taken for that change.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is defined as $\vec{a} = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \vec{v}}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of the velocity vector.

q: An object moving with constant speed along a curved path is ____ as the direction of the velocity is changing.
e: Even at constant speed, a change in the direction of velocity means the object is accelerating.

q: The direction of the velocity of the object is ____ to its path.
e: At any point on a curved path, the velocity vector is directed tangentially to the path.

q: Hence, the object is accelerated whenever the velocity changes in magnitude, ____, (or) both.
e: Acceleration occurs if there is a change in the magnitude of velocity, its direction, or both simultaneously.

q: An object moves in both x and y direction simultaneously is said to be undergoing ____ motion.
e: The summary reiterates that simultaneous motion in horizontal and vertical directions defines projectile motion.

q: Circular motion is a movement of an object along the ____ of a circle or rotation along a circular path.
e: The summary defines circular motion as movement constrained to the circumference of a circle.

q: Instantaneous angular velocity is defined as the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: This key definition is highlighted in the chapter summary.

q: Instantaneous angular acceleration is the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: This key definition is highlighted in the chapter summary.

q: A projectile is any object thrown into space upon which the only acting force is the ____.
e: In ideal projectile motion, air resistance is neglected, making gravity the sole acting force on the object.

q: The path followed by a projectile is known as a ____.
e: The trajectory is the specific curved path that a projectile follows through space.

q: The motion of an object moving in both horizontal x direction and vertical y direction simultaneously is called the ____.
e: Projectile motion is defined as two-dimensional motion where an object moves horizontally and vertically at the same time.

q: If air resistance is neglected, an object moves along the horizontal x direction with a constant ____ and in the vertical y direction with constant downward acceleration.
e: In the horizontal direction, there is no acceleration ($a_x = 0$), so the horizontal velocity remains constant.

q: In such case, only ____ force is acting on it.
e: When air resistance is neglected, the gravitational force is the only force acting on the projectile.

q: Therefore, the downward acceleration is the acceleration due to ____ which is a constant over the range of motion.
e: The constant downward acceleration in projectile motion is the acceleration due to gravity, denoted by g.

q: The vertical motion of projectile is a ____ motion.
e: Because the only vertical force is gravity, the vertical component of projectile motion is equivalent to free fall.

q: If the initial velocity makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal, the x and y components of the initial velocity are $v_{0x} = $ ____ and $v_{0y} = v_0 \sin \theta$.
e: The initial velocity is resolved into horizontal and vertical components using trigonometric functions.

q: In order to analyze the projectile motion, the motion can be considered into two parts, horizontal motion (x direction) and ____ motion (y direction).
e: Projectile motion is analyzed by treating the horizontal and vertical motions independently.

q: In x direction, $a_x = 0$ and $v_x = v_{0x} = $ ____ $= \text{constant}$.
e: The horizontal velocity remains constant throughout the flight because there is no horizontal acceleration.

q: The horizontal displacement of projectile can be written as a function of time; $x = v_{0x} t = $ ____.
e: Horizontal displacement is the product of the constant horizontal velocity and the time of flight.

q: In y direction, $v_{0y}$ is the initial velocity and $a_y$ is ____.
e: The vertical acceleration is negative because it acts in the downward direction, opposite to the conventional positive y-axis.

q: Since the acceleration along the vertical y direction is downward direction, g can be taken as ____ sign.
e: The negative sign indicates that the acceleration due to gravity acts downward.

q: The velocity of the projectile in the time t in the y direction is given by $v_y = v_{0y} + $ ____.
e: This is the first kinematic equation applied to the vertical component of projectile motion.

q: The relation between vertical velocity and displacement is $v_y^2 = v_{0y}^2 + $ ____.
e: This is the third kinematic equation, relating vertical velocity, initial vertical velocity, acceleration, and vertical displacement.

q: The vertical displacement of the projectile in time t is given by $y = v_{0y} t + $ ____.
e: This is the second kinematic equation applied to the vertical motion of the projectile.

q: The magnitude of the velocity of the projectile at any instant of time is, $v = $ ____.
e: The resultant velocity at any instant is found by combining the horizontal and vertical velocity components using the Pythagorean theorem.

q: The direction of the velocity of the projectile is given by $\tan \theta = $ ____.
e: The angle of the velocity vector with respect to the horizontal is determined by the ratio of the vertical to horizontal velocity components.

q: The projectile reaches the highest point when its vertical component of velocity ____ is zero.
e: At the maximum height, the projectile momentarily stops moving upward before descending, making its vertical velocity zero.

q: The time taken to reach the highest point is $t_1 = $ ____.
e: This is derived by setting the final vertical velocity to zero in the first kinematic equation and solving for time.

q: The ____ is twice the time to reach the maximum height.
e: Due to the symmetry of projectile motion, the total time of flight is exactly double the time taken to reach the peak.

q: The time of flight is given by $T = 2 t_1 = $ ____.
e: The total time of flight is calculated by doubling the time required to reach the maximum height.

q: The horizontal range R is the horizontal distance from the starting point to the point where the projectile returns to the same ____.
e: The horizontal range is measured from the launch point to the point where the projectile lands at its original vertical level.

q: The horizontal range is obtained as $R = v_{0x} T = $ ____.
e: The range is the product of the constant horizontal velocity and the total time of flight.

q: Using the trigonometric identity $2 \sin \theta \cos \theta = \sin 2\theta$, the horizontal range is simplified to $R = $ ____.
e: This simplified formula shows that the range depends on the square of the initial velocity and the sine of twice the launch angle.

q: Another case of the projectile motion is an object thrown ____.
e: In this specific case, the object has an initial horizontal velocity but no initial vertical velocity.

q: There is no vertical component to its initial velocity; that is, ____ $= 0$, $v_{0x} = v_0$.
e: For an object thrown horizontally, the entire initial velocity is directed along the x-axis.

q: The vertical velocity of the object in the time t is $v_y = $ ____.
e: Since the initial vertical velocity is zero, the vertical velocity at any time t is solely due to gravitational acceleration.

q: The vertical displacement in time t for an object thrown horizontally is, $y = $ ____.
e: This equation describes the downward free-fall distance of an object with zero initial vertical velocity.

q: Circular motion is a specific type of a ____ motion.
e: Circular motion occurs in a plane, making it a specific case of two-dimensional motion.

q: It is a movement of an object along the ____ of a circle (or) rotation along a circular path.
e: In circular motion, the object's path is constrained to the outer boundary or circumference of a circle.

q: We can experience a pulling force (known as the ____) exerted on the ball by the string.
e: When whirling a ball on a string, the string exerts a tension force that keeps the ball in circular motion.

q: Other examples of the circular motion are a satellite orbiting the earth, motion of a wheel, turning of a car around ____ respectively.
e: A car turning follows a curved path, which is a practical example of circular motion in everyday life.

q: If an object (rigid body) rotates about an axis, each particle consisting of the object moves in a ____ motion.
e: In a rotating rigid body, every individual particle traces out a circular path around the axis of rotation.

q: Although an object moves in a circle at a constant speed, its ____ is not constant.
e: Velocity is a vector quantity, so even if the speed is constant, the continuously changing direction means the velocity is not constant.

q: The direction of the velocity is ____ to the path.
e: At any given point in circular motion, the velocity vector points tangent to the circular path.

q: Velocity is constantly changing because the ____ of the velocity is changing continuously.
e: The continuous change in the direction of motion is what causes the velocity to change, resulting in acceleration.

q: The velocity in circular motion is also called the ____ velocity.
e: Because it is always directed tangent to the circular path, the linear velocity in circular motion is referred to as tangential velocity.

q: In this time interval, it has rotated through an angle $\theta$ with respect to the reference line and through a distance s measured along the circumference of the circle, called an ____ length.
e: The distance traveled along the curved path of the circle is known as the arc length.

q: Change of the angular position is called the angular ____.
e: Angular displacement measures the angle through which an object has rotated from its initial reference position.

q: The angular displacement is the ratio of the arc length to ____.
e: By definition, angular displacement in radians is the arc length divided by the radius of the circle.

q: The magnitude of angular displacement ($\theta$), measured in radian (rad), is given by $\theta = $ ____.
e: This formula defines the radian measure of an angle as the ratio of the subtended arc length to the radius.

q: One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the ____ of the circle.
e: This is the fundamental geometric definition of one radian.

q: If $s = r$, $\theta = $ ____.
e: When the arc length equals the radius, the angular displacement is exactly one radian.
One full revolution around a circle corresponds to an angle of $2\pi$ radians.

q: Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to ____ taken.
e: Average angular velocity measures how much angular displacement occurs per unit of time.

q: Average angular velocity is given by $\omega_{avg} = \frac{\theta_2 - \theta_1}{t_2 - t_1} = $ ____.
e: This is the standard formula for calculating average angular velocity over a finite time interval.

q: If the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the instantaneous angular velocity can be written as $\omega = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \theta}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous angular velocity is the first derivative of angular displacement with respect to time.

q: At constant angular velocity, $\omega = $ ____.
e: When angular velocity is constant, it can be simply calculated as the total angular displacement divided by the total time.

q: Angular velocity is measured in radian per second (rad s$^{-1}$), revolution per second (rps) and revolution per ____ (rpm or rev min$^{-1}$).
e: Revolutions per minute (rpm) is a common practical unit for measuring angular velocity, especially in machinery.

q: The average angular acceleration is the ratio of change of angular velocity to ____ taken.
e: Average angular acceleration measures the rate at which angular velocity changes over a given time period.

q: The average angular acceleration is given by $\alpha_{avg} = \frac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{t_2 - t_1} = $ ____.
e: This formula calculates the average rate of change of angular velocity.

q: If the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the instantaneous angular acceleration can be defined as $\alpha = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \omega}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous angular acceleration is the first derivative of angular velocity with respect to time.

q: The instantaneous angular acceleration is the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: This is the formal definition of instantaneous angular acceleration.

q: When a body is moving with a constant angular acceleration, $\alpha = $ ____.
e: For constant angular acceleration, it is calculated as the change in angular velocity divided by the time taken.

q: Angular acceleration is measured in radian per second squared (rad s$^{-2}$) and revolution per ____ squared (rev s$^{-2}$).
e: The standard SI unit for angular acceleration is radians per second squared.

q: The magnitude of the angular velocity (angular speed) is related to that of the ____ velocity (tangential speed) as follows.
e: There is a direct proportional relationship between angular speed and tangential speed for a given radius.

q: Since $r$ is constant, the relation between tangential speed and angular speed is $v = $ ____.
e: Tangential velocity is the product of the radius of the circular path and the angular velocity.

q: The relation between the angular acceleration $\alpha$ and the tangential acceleration $a_t$ is $a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = $ ____.
e: Tangential acceleration is the time derivative of tangential velocity.

q: Since $r$ is constant, the relation simplifies to $a_t = $ ____.
e: Tangential acceleration is the product of the radius and the angular acceleration.

q: In Eq.(1.17), the direction of linear acceleration $a_t$ is ____ to the path.
e: Tangential acceleration acts along the tangent to the circular path, changing the speed of the object.

q: It is called the ____ acceleration.
e: This component of acceleration is specifically named for its direction tangent to the circular path.
